ageing_relevance.rationale: About 10% of B2M papers concern ageing, and it is a GrimAge component protein. There are no ageing-disease associations and MR could not be tested, so there is no genetic causal evidence.

evidence.value: not tested: no cis instruments (p < 5e-8 within 1 Mb of the gene; 1 genome-wide). Untested is not a null result.

One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up the GrimAge clock. Part 1 of this project: the GrimAge clock as a whole was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia, a difference that disappeared after adjusting for a methylation smoking score; this protein's own surrogate was not tested. Surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels. Shirai et al. 2024 (7-cohort meta-analysis): this protein's DNAm surrogate was higher in schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis in a model adjusted for age, sex and DNAm smoking pack-years.

background_knowledge: Circulating B2M is reported to rise with age and has been linked in mouse studies to cognitive decline (observational/preclinical).

mechanism.rationale: B2M's function as an MHC class I component is well characterised. Its causal link to ageing and the direction of modulation are not established, because MR was not tested and the project findings concern the methylation surrogate, not the measured protein.

evidence.value: Component of the class I major histocompatibility complex (MHC). Involved in the presentation of peptide antigens to the immune system.
not tested: no cis instruments (p < 5e-8 within 1 Mb of the gene; 1 genome-wide). Untested is not a null result.

tractability.rationale: Open Targets lists a small-molecule ligand-bound structure with a high-quality pocket. It also lists antibody-feasible features for a secreted/cell-surface protein and PROTAC features. There is no approved-drug precedence.

safety.rationale: No liabilities are recorded, but absence of data is not evidence of safety. Disease associations show that loss of function causes MHC class I deficiency, which suggests immune risk from systemic inhibition.
background_knowledge: B2M is required for surface MHC class I expression, so broad inhibition could impair antigen presentation and immune surveillance.

clinical_precedence.rationale: No drugs acting on B2M are listed in the clinic.

assessment.summary: B2M is a secreted and cell-surface MHC class I component. It is one of the GrimAge plasma proteins, and about 10% of its literature concerns ageing. Open Targets lists no ageing-disease associations, and MR was not tested because no cis instruments were available, so causal direction is unknown. Tractability is moderate (small-molecule pocket, antibody and PROTAC features), but there are no clinical candidates. No safety liabilities are listed, but the MHC class I deficiency association suggests a possible immune risk. Recommendation: consider.
key_uncertainties: No MR evidence, so it is unknown whether genetically higher B2M worsens ageing; a non-cis instrument or an alternative proteomic study could resolve this.
Project findings concern the DNAm surrogate, not the measured protein.
Whether lowering circulating B2M (as opposed to cell-surface MHC I function) can be done selectively and safely.
source_conflicts: Tractability lists small-molecule, antibody and PROTAC features, but the clinical candidates list shows no drugs. I relied on the clinical list for precedence.
